# [TASK] Implement Actor Service

## Task
Implement Actor Service with TMDB API integration for cast/crew details, filmography, images, and search — served as a TMDB-compatible facade backed by actor-service's own persisted PostgreSQL catalog (own the data, don't proxy it — ADR-010).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] TMDB-compatible facade implemented — `/person/{id}`, `/movie_credits`, `/images`, `/popular`, `/search/person`; details and images are read-through/save-through PostgreSQL
- [x] Native `/api/v1/actors` API implemented with paginated filmography and HATEOAS links
- [x] Registered with Eureka, health checks and OpenAPI docs passing
- [x] Caching verified live — repeat calls served from PostgreSQL in single-digit ms with zero TMDB calls
- [x] Tests passing at 85%+ coverage — 28/28 green (Mockito unit tests + TestContainers/WireMock integration tests)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 6-8

## Notes
- Architecture pivoted from a raw TMDB passthrough (ADR-003) to owning persisted, typed data behind a TMDB-shaped facade (ADR-010) — see `docs/architecture/adr/`.
- Real commits: `4300030` (2026-07-21, initial build), `69755bc` (2026-07-23, audit closed 3 missing endpoints, a 500-on-bad-id defect, and restored a deleted unit-test layer).
- No actor↔movie join table — movies live in movie-service's own database (ADR-002). MapStruct not used; mapping is hand-written, same call as user-service (#17).
